passages.title: Marrow Point lighthouse
passages.text: The Marrow Point lighthouse was built in 1874 from grey granite quarried nearby. Its lamp was converted from oil to electricity in 1952, and the keeper's cottage was sold the following decade.

passages.title: Hartley's bakery
passages.text: Hartley's bakery opens at five each morning. Its sourdough uses a starter that the founder's grandmother began in 1931, fed daily with rye flour. The shop closes on Mondays.

passages.title: The Number 9 tram
passages.text: The Number 9 tram links the station with the university every eight minutes during term time. A single fare costs two pounds forty, and children under seven travel free.

passages.title: Community orchard
passages.text: The community orchard has forty-two apple trees, mostly Bramley and Cox varieties. Volunteers prune in February and the harvest festival is held on the first Saturday of October.

passages.title: Hilltop observatory
passages.text: The hilltop observatory houses a refracting telescope with a 15-inch lens. Public viewing nights run on the second Friday of each month, weather permitting.

passages.title: The canal
passages.text: The canal was dug by hand in the 1790s to carry coal to the mills. It is eleven miles long and has fourteen locks, the deepest of which drops three metres.

passages.title: Town library
passages.text: The town library lends tools as well as books. Members can borrow drills, ladders and sewing machines for up to two weeks, and there is a waiting list for the pressure washer.

passages.title: The 1987 flood
passages.text: In the flood of 1987 the river rose four metres in one night. Sandbags were stacked outside the market hall and sixty families were housed in the school gymnasium.

passages.title: Wednesday choir
passages.text: The Wednesday choir rehearses at seven in the church hall. New members are welcome without an audition, and the winter concert raises money for the food bank.

passages.title: The iron footbridge
passages.text: The iron footbridge over the weir was repaired in 2019 after inspectors found cracks in two of its supports. It reopened in March, painted dark green.
